records.name: Alaska
records.summary: Moderate tier in the July 2026 legal-risk assessment (grouped with Kentucky and North Carolina): one or two laws aimed at transgender adults or several aimed at youth, but no adult facility ban recorded and no protective statute. Slightly below the national score 0.36.

records.name: Georgia
records.summary:
A July 2026 data analysis places Georgia's recorded killing rate for trans women at 4.8 per 100k per year — among the country's highest — and a Georgia law-review article documents the long-run fatality concentration around Atlanta: at least 15 fatal cases statewide across 1990–2014 (11 in Atlanta) and 16 more across 2015–2023 (8 in Atlanta). Both series are treated by their authors as undercount floors.

The same analysis's warning applies to Georgia directly: its legal-risk grade describes how the state behaves, not how its people do — here a jurisdiction whose documented danger to trans people has been violence on the street more than legislation from the legislature.

records.name: New Hampshire
records.summary: Highest per-capita incident load in the country: 72 recorded anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025 in a state of ~1.4m. Counterweight: in July 2026 a county court found an attacker violated the NH Civil Rights Act after striking a trans gas-station employee, using his pronoun refusal as bias evidence, with bodycam showing officers correcting his pronoun use — institutions working. Slightly below the national score 0.36.

records.name: Arizona
records.summary:
A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places Arizona among its 'low-risk states' group: it has largely refrained from targeting transgender adults, and although it has enacted policies affecting trans youth, the map's author considers them unlikely to be extended to adults. That is the assessment's praise of restraint, not of protection — no extraordinary protective measures are recorded for Arizona.

The local scene has tracked the national chill: Tucson cancelled its historic 2026 Pride celebration, citing a political and financial environment that made hosting nearly impossible and attending potentially unsafe.

records.name: Virginia
records.summary:
A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places Virginia among its 'low-risk states' group — largely refraining from targeting transgender adults — while noting Virginia has enacted anti-trans policies affecting trans youth that the map's author considers unlikely to be extended to adults.

The state's school-focused facility restriction (2023) is recorded in a national equality tracker, though the tracker's cited page has since moved; the practical exposure for a visitor in Virginia therefore sits with the youth-policy record rather than any statute aimed at adult public life.

records.name: District of Columbia
records.summary: Downgraded from “most protective”: as a federal district, Congress and the executive reach it directly — Congress attached a bathroom ban for DC, and activists protesting it at the Capitol were arrested (Dec 2024). Its protective local-law layer persists but is overridable; direction: mixed, downgraded from its former most-protective placement.

freshness.fact: Cited Dec 2024 Capitol bathroom-protest arrests are historical record (do not stale); DC itself has no ban and protective code unchanged.

evidence.title: Axios: activists arrested at Capitol bathroom-ban protest

records.name: Maine
records.summary: Assessed comparatively protected (low-risk tier, July 2026) — but rose in risk after the University of Maine system capitulated to federal pressure on trans sports participation rather than defending its trans students and athletes: the system affirmed compliance with the new federal rules once the Department of Agriculture suspended its federal funding (March 2025). Direction: better than the country overall, with an upward risk signal.

records.name: Delaware
records.summary:
A July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places Delaware in its 'low-risk states' group — states that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection; nothing in Delaware's record rises above that description in either direction.

A national equality tracker records no public-facility-use ban for Delaware. A September 2026 status check likewise found no enacted facility ban, while flagging that the tracker's own citation (a page since relocated) still awaits one manual re-verification.

freshness.fact: No enacted facility ban found on the Delaware state page; MAP-listing citation cannot be matched to a specific Delaware claim without the original text. Needs manual verification.
